## 9. Telemetry

Every full build and every cache event appends one JSON line to
`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, per `DESIGN.md`'s telemetry contract.

```jsonc
{"ts": "<ISO 8601 with offset>",
 "kind": "warm" | "rebuild" | "cache-get",
 "trigger": "<who asked for this>",
 "outcome": "success" | "failed",
 "seconds": <int>,
 "sha": "<commit, when known>",
 "note": "<sanitized, ≤400 chars>"}
```

* `warm` — a warmer build and publish.
* `rebuild` — a consumer's full `lake build` (cold path, or `--build`).
* `cache-get` — a per-worktree tier-2 fetch.

Three properties are load-bearing:

* **The primary checkout owns the file.** Even when invoked from a linked
  worktree, the scripts resolve `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` back to the
  primary repository, so an append-only JSONL does not fork per worktree and
  produce merge conflicts. Override with `MIPSTARRE_TELEMETRY_DIR`.
* **Appends are serialized** by a short-lived `mkdir` lock, and give up after 5 s
  rather than delaying a build. Telemetry never blocks or fails a build; every
  failure path degrades to a warning.
* **`note` is sanitized** — non-printable characters stripped, truncated to 400
  characters — because notes may quote build output, and compiler output is
  untrusted text regardless of where it was produced (`DESIGN.md` #6).

## 10. Operating procedures

```bash
# Seed or refresh the hot main cache (do this after every merge to main).
local/bin/cache-warmer.sh --ref main

# What is published right now?
local/bin/cache-warmer.sh --status

# Bootstrap a brand-new agent worktree end to end.
local/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/.worktrees/issue-0042-qpbt-basis

# Verify an existing worktree without touching it.
local/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/worktree --check

# Re-warm a worktree after the warmer published a newer snapshot.
local/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --force

# What would this worktree do, warm or cold?
local/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --status
```

After a toolchain or Mathlib bump lands on `main`, the ordering is fixed: **warm
first, adopt second.** The bump changes the keyhash, so every existing snapshot
is invalid and every worktree cold-paths until a fresh snapshot exists. Run
`cache-warmer.sh --ref main` before dispatching agents, or pay for a full build in
each worktree serialized behind one lock.

---

## 11. Failure modes and how each degrades

| condition | behaviour |
|---|---|
| No snapshot published yet | Warn, name the warmer command, take the cold path. |
| Keyhash mismatch | Warn with both hashes, take the cold path. Never a partial reuse. |
| Malformed / unreadable `STAMP` | Treated as *no snapshot*; cold path. |
| Snapshot is `partial` | Used, with a warning naming the SHA that failed. |
| `cp -c` unsupported (non-APFS, cross-volume) | Warn, fall back to `cp -R`. Correct, just slower and larger. |
| `lake exe cache get` fails | Warn; tier 2 gets compiled from source. Non-fatal. |
| Full-build lock held | Wait; the warmer waits indefinitely by default, consumers time out per `--lock-timeout`. |
| Stale lock (dead pid, or age > TTL) | Broken by atomic rename, with a warning naming the dead holder. |
| Primary repo has no commits on `main` | Hard error naming the cause. Never a silent no-op. |
| `warm-worktree.sh` missing during bootstrap | Hard error. `--skip-warm` is the explicit opt-out. |
| `origin/main` does not resolve | Warning, non-zero exit from `--check`, because hooks self-disable silently. |
| `python3` absent | Warmer: hard error (needed for the atomic publish). Consumer: warning, telemetry skipped. |

## 13. Invariant checklist

A change to any of these scripts must preserve all of the following:

1. Only `cache-warmer.sh` writes into `hot-main/`. Consumers refuse to run there.
2. `compute_keyhash` is byte-identical across both scripts.
3. A snapshot becomes visible only via `rename(2)`, fully built and stamped.
4. `current` is re-pointed only via `rename(2)` over the symlink — never `mv`.
5. Consumers resolve `current` exactly once per run.
6. Keyhash mismatch → cold path. Never a partial or best-effort reuse.
7. Failed builds still publish, flagged `partial`.
8. GC never removes the snapshot `current` names.
9. At most one full `lake build` machine-wide; `lake env lean` takes no lock.
10. `.lake/packages` is a symlink to the read-only store `$CACHE_ROOT/packages/<key>`;
    the store is `chmod a-w`; no automated `lake update`.
11. The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround runs before any `lake exe cache get`.
12. Every `lake` / vendored-`git` invocation goes through `run_outside_git_env`.
13. `STAMP` is parsed by whitelist and validated; never `eval`ed or `source`d.
14. Telemetry is best-effort, serialized, sanitized, and lands in the primary checkout.
15. Every degradation is a loud warning or a hard error. Never a silent no-op.
# Protocol — local PR CI

Normative protocol for `local/bin/ci.sh`, the local replacement for
`.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml` (frozen under `.github/`, never executed here).
Read `meta.md` first; `build-cache.md` owns the hot-main cache this protocol
consumes but never writes.

`ci.sh <pr-number>` is the **only** thing allowed to publish the `local-ci/*`
commit statuses. Everything downstream — `review.sh` (invariant 2: review only
after green CI on the same head SHA), `autofix.sh` (invariant 3: sync/audit
failures are never auto-fixed), and the merge gate in `pr_merge.py` — reads
those exact-head statuses and the manifest comment this script publishes
(`local/protocols/issues-prs.md` §2), and nothing else.

## 1. What it is

The parent repository consolidated seven workflows into one so that a pull
request produces exactly **one** CI completion event, which the auto-fix
dispatcher keys off (`pr-ci.yml:3-8`). The local port keeps that property: one
invocation, one manifest, one exit code.

```
local/bin/ci.sh <pr-id> [--worktree PATH] [--base REF] [--only STEP]
                        [--force-all] [--skip-build] [--dry-run]
```

`<pr-id>` is the GitHub PR number; the script reads `branch`, `base` and the
head SHA from GitHub (`gh_common.py pr-view`), finds the branch's worktree (via
`git worktree list`, falling back to `.worktrees/<branch with / → ->`), and
runs everything **inside that worktree**. Nothing is run in the primary
checkout, and the worktree's branch tip must equal the remote head before the
run starts.

Exit status: `0` all gating steps passed or were legitimately skipped; `1` at
least one gating step failed or could not run; `2` the run could not start
(unknown PR number, missing worktree, unresolvable base, GitHub unreachable —
a GitHub error never degrades to a local record).

### Preconditions that are hard errors, never silent skips

| Precondition | Why it is fatal |
|---|---|
| GitHub returns an open PR with a head branch | there is no branch to test |
| a worktree for that branch exists | CI must not test the primary checkout |
| `origin/<base>` or `<base>` resolves | invariant 8 — the diff-based audits and the change gating self-disable without a base, which is exactly the "checks silently stopped running" failure the parent repo patched twice |
| a merge base exists | the change set is undefined without one |
| `python3` on `PATH` | every audit job and the manifest writer need it |

There is deliberately **no `LOCAL_CI_ENABLED` kill switch**. `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED`
and `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` exist because a disabled reviewer or fixer merely
stops work from happening; a disabled CI would hand the merge gate a green
light it never earned. If CI must not run, do not run it — the head SHA simply
keeps whatever statuses it already carries.

## 2. Job table

Eight steps, in this order, named exactly after the parent workflow's job ids
so the auto-fix dispatcher's mapping (build → ci-fix, blueprint-render →
blueprint-fix, everything else → never auto-fixed) ports without translation.

| Step | Parent job | What it runs (in the worktree) | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| `build` | `build` (`pr-ci.yml:115-168`) | warm `.lake/build`, `lake exe cache get`, `lake build`, `lake build MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit` (`:155-156`), `scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py` (`:158-159`) | `lean ∨ comparator ∨ workflow` |
| `blueprint-render` | `blueprint-render` (`:173-243`) | `leanblueprint pdf` + non-empty `blueprint/print/print.pdf` (`:210-218`), `texra-blueprint bbl` (`:222-223`), `texra-blueprint web` with `grep '^ERROR:'` (`:225-243`) | `blueprint_src ∨ workflow` |
| `paper-gaps` | `paper-gaps` (`:248-271`) | `texra-blueprint --root . paper-gaps check` | `paper_gaps ∨ workflow` |
| `blueprint-sync` | `blueprint-sync` (`:273-317`) | `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`, `blueprint_lean_sync.py --update-lean-decls`, `blueprint_lean_sync.py --ci`, `blueprint_axiom_audit_needed.py --base-ref` | `lean ∨ blueprint ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
| `file-length` | `file-length` (`:319-340`) | `check_oversized_lean_files.py --root .` (>1000 lines) | `mip_lean ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
| `proof-debt` | `proof-debt` (`:342-386`) | `unittest test_audit_paper_facing_proof_debt.py`, `audit_paper_facing_proof_debt.py --ci` | `mip_lean ∨ tex_chapter ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
| `proof-evasion` | `proof-evasion` (`:388-445`) | four regression tests, then `audit_lean_axiom_declarations.py --ci`, `audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py --ci`, `audit_unfaithful_markers.py --ci`, and `check_duplicate_private_helpers.py --ci` (advisory) | `mip_lean ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
| `statement-origin` | `statement-origin` (`:447-487`) | `check_statement_paper_origin.py --root .` | `ldt_lean ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |

Every step is blocking. The single advisory sub-check is
`check_duplicate_private_helpers.py`: exit 1 means "candidates reported" and is
downgraded to a warning, any other nonzero status is a real failure — the same
`set +e` dance as `pr-ci.yml:432-445`.

Two GitHub-only behaviours are dropped on purpose: `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`
blocks and `::error` / `::notice` / `::warning` annotations are inert outside
Actions, so the step's stdout+stderr log **is** the summary. `--github-annotations`
is not passed to `check_duplicate_private_helpers.py`. Exit-code semantics are
preserved exactly: `::warning` never failed a job, and the `^ERROR:` grep
always did.

### Steps that did not run

A step whose area did not change is recorded `skipped` with the reason — never
omitted. A skipped step is green for the merge gate, exactly as a skipped
GitHub job is. This is why the gating globs are load-bearing (§3): a glob that
under-matches turns a real gate into a permanent, invisible `skipped`.

## 3. Gating globs — keep in lockstep

`git diff --name-only --no-renames <merge-base> <head>` replaces
`dorny/paths-filter@v3`. `--no-renames` is deliberate: reporting both the old
and the new path means a rename *out of* a gated tree still trips that tree's
filter, and deletions count. `*` in these patterns spans `/`, matching
minimatch's `**`.

| Area | Globs | Parent |
|---|---|---|
| `lean` | `*.lean`, `lakefile.*`, `lean-toolchain`, `lake-manifest.json` | `pr-ci.yml:84-88` |
| `mip_lean` | `MIPStarRE/*.lean` | `:89-90` |
| `ldt_lean` | `MIPStarRE/LDT/*.lean` | `:91-92` |
| `blueprint` | `blueprint/*` | `:93-94` |
| `blueprint_src` | `blueprint/src/*` | `:95-96` |
| `tex_chapter` | `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` | `:97-98` |
| `paper_gaps` | `docs/paper-gaps/*`, `texra-blueprint.toml`, `MIPStarRE/*.lean`, `blueprint/src/*`, `docs/*.md` | `:99-107` |
| `scripts` | `scripts/*` | `:108-109` |
| `comparator` | `scripts/comparator/*` | `:110-111` |
| `workflow` | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml`, `local/bin/*`, `local/protocols/*`, `.githooks/*` | `:112-113`, extended |

> **Lockstep warning.** These globs must move together with the trees the audit
> scripts actually scan. The parent repo patched the `paper_gaps` filter twice
> after checks silently never ran — the note at `pr-ci.yml:102-104` is the scar.
> The failure mode is asymmetric: an over-broad glob costs CPU, an under-broad
> glob costs a merged regression that no check ever looked at. When you widen
> a scan tree in `scripts/*.py`, widen the matching glob in `ci.sh` in the same
> commit, per `meta.md` §5.

The `workflow` area is the one deliberate extension. On GitHub it meant "the
workflow file changed, so re-run everything"; locally the workflow layer is a
whole tree — the frozen reference `pr-ci.yml`, every driver and helper under
`local/bin/`, every protocol under `local/protocols/`, and the hooks in
`.githooks/` — and a change to any of them forces a full run, every step
included. The globs are that broad on purpose: a `gh_common.py`-only change has
to run the `scripts/tests` unit suite that covers it — carried by
`blueprint-sync` — and under the old three-file glob such a change matched no
area and ran nothing at all (PR 7 review, F13).

## 4. Manifest schema

Built in runtime storage (same-directory tempfile + `os.replace`) and then
posted as the manifest PR comment (§5):

```
~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.json          complete run
~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.partial.json  partial run
```

A run is **partial** when it was given `--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`;
`--dry-run` writes nothing at all.

Step logs live outside the repository, under
`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/<pr-id>/<head_sha>/<step>.log`.

```jsonc
{
  "schema": 1,
  "generator": "local/bin/ci.sh",
  "replaces": ".github/workflows/pr-ci.yml",
  "pr": 7,                       // GitHub PR number
  "branch": "issue-7-qpbt-basis",
  "base": "main",                // from the GitHub PR
  "base_ref": "origin/main",     // what actually resolved
  "merge_base": "<sha>",
  "head_sha": "<sha>",           // the SHA every step ran against
  "worktree": "/abs/path",
  "started": "2026-08-30T09:23:07+0800",   // ISO-8601 with offset
  "finished": "2026-08-30T09:41:52+0800",
  "seconds": 1125,               // whole run, integer
  "conclusion": "success",       // success | failure | error
  "partial": false,              // true ⇒ not a merge-gate verdict
  "areas": { "lean": true, "blueprint_src": false, ... },
  "changed_files": ["MIPStarRE/Quantum/PauliBasis.lean", ...],
  "warnings": ["texra-blueprint not installed; skipped ...", ...],
  "steps": [
    {
      "step": "build",           // one of the eight job ids, always all eight
      "outcome": "success",      // success | failure | error | skipped
      "seconds": 883,
      "log_path": "/Users/…/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/0007/<sha>/build.log",
      "blocking": true,
      "note": ""                 // skip reason, exit code, or degradation cause
    }
  ]
}
```

Outcome vocabulary — the distinction is what routes the auto-fix loop:

| `outcome` | Meaning | Auto-fix |
|---|---|---|
| `success` | the step ran and passed | — |
| `failure` | the step ran and the code is wrong | `build` → ci-fix, `blueprint-render` → blueprint-fix, everything else → **never** |
| `error` | the step could not run (missing tool, unbootstrapped worktree, build lock unavailable) | never — this is an operator problem, not a code problem |
| `skipped` | gated out, or excluded by `--only` / `--skip-build` | — |

`conclusion` is `failure` if any step failed, else `error` if any step errored,
else `success`. The run's exit status is `0` iff `conclusion == "success"`.

## 5. Publication

Evidence goes to GitHub, bound to the exact SHA the steps ran against
(`issues-prs.md` §2). For every complete run:

* one `local-ci/<step>` status per gate step — `pending` posted before the
  step, then `success | failure | error`; a gated-out step is a `success`
  whose description says it was skipped, so the gate never has to distinguish
  "absent" from "not applicable";
* `local-ci/summary` carrying the run's `conclusion`;
* the manifest JSON as the PR comment marked
  `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, created or updated in place.

`pending` before the first step is the old `ci_status: running`: a crashed,
killed or power-cut run leaves `pending`, never a stale `success`, so the
review gate's "green CI on the same head SHA" check (invariant 2) fails closed.
Immediately before the final publication `ci.sh` re-reads both the local branch
tip and the remote PR head; if either moved, it publishes no success and exits
nonzero, because a status is a claim about one commit.

A **partial** run (`--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`) publishes nothing at
all — no statuses, no manifest comment — and keeps its manifest in runtime
storage only. `--base` belongs on that list because an overridden base (the PR
head, say) can empty the diff and mark every gate skipped-success. Partial runs
are a debugging aid; they must not be able to produce a merge-gate verdict, and
they must not clobber a complete manifest for the same SHA.

## 6. Concurrency and locks

Two advisory `mkdir`-based lease directories, both under
`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/` (`MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT` overrides the root). Each
holds an `owner` file: pid, ISO timestamp, tag. A lock is broken only when its
owner pid is dead or its stamp is older than `MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S`
(default 3 h).

| Lock | Scope | On contention |
|---|---|---|
| `locks/ci-<pr-id>.lock` | one `ci.sh` per PR | **refuse immediately** (exit 2) |
| `$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock` | one full `lake build` machine-wide (invariant 7) | wait up to `MIPSTARRE_CI_BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S` (default 4 h), then record `build` as `error` and continue with the Python steps |

Only the `build` step takes the full-build lock. The audits are pure Python and
take nothing; single-file `lake env lean` checks are read-only over oleans and
take nothing either — which is precisely why `.githooks/pre-push` can use them
per-file without serializing.

`ci.sh` never cancels a running build. GitHub cancels in-progress PR runs
(`pr-ci.yml:48-51`) because its runners are disposable and main-branch runs —
the ones that seed the cache — are exempt. Locally there is nothing disposable:
killing a build mid-flight leaves a half-written `.lake/build` and a held lease.
So a second run for the same PR is refused, and a foreign live build lease is
waited on, never stolen. Do not `kill -9` a running `ci.sh`; if you must, remove
the lease directories by hand.

## 7. Build step and the two-tier cache

`build` is the only step that touches the cache, and it only ever **reads** the
shared tree. This is the local translation of the parent's main-only cache save
policy, whose rationale is documented at `pr-ci.yml:137-142`: per-PR saves of
~2.6 GB cycled through the 10 GB repository budget and evicted the main entry,
so no run ever restored usable oleans. The local failure mode is identical if a
worktree writes into the shared snapshot, so it does not.

1. If `.lake/build` is absent, run `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh <worktree>`,
   which resolves the hot-main snapshot and clones it copy-on-write. Contract:
   idempotent, exit 0 when it populated or deliberately declined, nonzero on a
   hard error.
   - warmer missing → loud warning, cold build (still correct, just slow);
     set `MIPSTARRE_CI_REQUIRE_WARMER=1` to make it an `error` instead.
2. `.lake/build` (this project's oleans, per-worktree, writable) and
   `.lake/packages` (Mathlib and friends) are **different tiers** and are never
   conflated. If `.lake/packages` is a symlink it points at the shared hot-main
   dependency tree and is read-only: `lake exe cache get` is **skipped**,
   because it writes there. If it is a real directory, `lake exe cache get`
   runs, mirroring what `lean-action` does inside the parent job. Never run
   `lake update` in a consumer worktree.
3. `.lake/packages` absent entirely → `error`, pointing at
   `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh`. That bootstrap path is where the ProofWidgets
   prune workaround lives, and a package-free tree is exactly the state that
   triggers it. `MIPSTARRE_CI_ALLOW_COLD_FETCH=1` overrides for a tree you know
   is clean.
4. `lake build`, then `lake build MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`, then the
   comparator drift check.

Every `lake` and `python3` invocation goes through a subshell that unsets
`git rev-parse --local-env-vars` first. Inherited `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`
make Lake resolve nested package repositories against the wrong repository;
`.githooks/pre-push:19-24` does the same thing for the same reason, and any
orchestrator that invokes `ci.sh` from inside a git hook inherits the problem.

Lake's staleness is trace-hash-based, not mtime-based, so a restored snapshot
older than the merge base is safe — but only within one
`hash(lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, lakefile.toml)` class. Crossing that
boundary is `build-cache.md`'s problem, not this protocol's: `ci.sh` delegates
the check to `warm-worktree.sh` and simply builds whatever it is handed.

## 8. The axiom audit is reported, not run

`blueprint-sync` deliberately has no Lean setup. On GitHub that was forced by
repeated runner disk exhaustion, and the job degraded to a `::notice` telling a
human to run the audit locally (`pr-ci.yml:303-317`). Locally the constraint is
different but the conclusion is the same: the machine has a single full-build
budget, already spent by `build`. So `blueprint_axiom_audit_needed.py` runs, and
when it answers `true` the run records a warning:

> run `python3 scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py --ci` in a Lean environment

De-automation of this kind is a legitimate evolution step (`meta.md` §4), and
this one is inherited rather than invented.

## 9. Telemetry

When `build` actually ran (any outcome but `skipped`), one line is appended to
`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`:

```json
{"ts":"…","kind":"ci-build","trigger":"ci.sh pr=0007","seconds":883,
 "outcome":"success","sha":"…","note":"branch issue-7-qpbt-basis"}
```

This satisfies the `meta.md` duty that every full build be accounted for, and
makes "how much wall time did CI cost this PR" answerable by a script. The
per-step seconds in the manifest are the finer-grained record.

## 10. Trust boundary

Two things about `ci.sh` are worth stating plainly.

**It executes branch-authored code.** The audit scripts, the test suite, and
`lakefile.toml` all come from the worktree under test, because that is what CI
means and what the parent workflow did. Never run `ci.sh` on a branch you would
not run a shell script from.

**Its logs are untrusted data.** Compiler diagnostics, plasTeX output and test
failures can contain arbitrary text, including text shaped like instructions.
`ci.sh` stores logs verbatim and makes no attempt to clean them. Any consumer
that feeds a log into an agent prompt — `autofix.sh` above all — owes the
sanitization required by invariant 6: strip control characters, break fences,
truncate, and frame the payload as data that must not be followed. The manifest
gives consumers `log_path` rather than log content precisely so this stays the
consumer's explicit, visible responsibility.

## 11. Deliberate deviations from the parent workflow

| Parent | Local | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, `::error`/`::notice`/`::warning` | per-step log file + `warnings` array | inert outside Actions; exit codes carry all gating meaning |
| `cancel-in-progress` for PR runs | second run refused, running builds never killed | local build state is not disposable |
| cache `restore`/`save` actions | hot-main snapshot read via `warm-worktree.sh`; `ci.sh` never writes the shared cache | invariant 1 — the eviction failure documented at `pr-ci.yml:137-142` |
| `workflow` filter = the YAML file | also `local/bin/ci.sh`, `local/protocols/ci.md` | the CI definition is now three files |
| `--github-annotations` on the duplicate-helper audit | dropped | annotation-only flag |
| `push`-to-main and docs-only `pull_request` triggers | none | the docs-only paths existed solely to emit the completion event that started PR Review (`pr-ci.yml:31-33`); locally the lifecycle script calls `review.sh` directly |
| implicit "PR event" job conditions | every run is a PR run | `ci.sh` is only ever invoked on a GitHub PR number |

## 12. Amendments

Changing a gating glob, a step's command set, the manifest schema, the status
contexts or their vocabulary, or a lock's name or semantics is an amendment:
record the trigger in `results/telemetry/events.md`, edit this file and
`ci.sh` together, append to `EVOLUTION.md`, and grep `local/` for every other
enforcement point (`meta.md` §5). The manifest schema in particular is a
contract with `review.sh`, `autofix.sh` and `pr_merge.py`; bump `schema` when
it changes incompatibly.

blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex-70-\begin{remark}[Choice of decoding map and the decoder--encoder identity]\label{rem:qld-decoding-identity}
blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:71:	The source states the constructions of this chapter in terms of its boolean decoding map (the case $H = \{0,1\}$ of Definition~\ref{def:decoding-map}) while describing that map as returning the string of \emph{all} evaluations of $g$ on the hypercube. The proofs require the latter reading, $H = \F_q$, which is adopted throughout this chapter: the linearity of $\mathrm{Dec}$ and the identity $\mathrm{Dec}(g_h) = h$ for all $h \in \F_q^{M}$, both of which fail for the boolean map, are used in the symmetry step of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}. The source further asserts the identity $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u) = g(u)$ for every $g \in \mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$. Since the left-hand side equals $g_{\mathrm{Dec}(g)}(u)$, the identity, taken for all $u \in \F_q^m$, states that the multilinear representative $g_{\mathrm{Dec}(g)}$ and $g$ induce the same function on $\F_q^m$. Every encoding satisfies it, because then $g_{\mathrm{Dec}(g)} = g$ as polynomial representatives; a polynomial that is not an encoding need not: for $m = 1$, $d \geq 2$, and $q > 2$, the polynomial $g(x) = x^2$ has $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_1(u) = u$, which differs from $g(u) = u^2$ at every $u \notin \{0,1\}$. When $d \leq q-1$ the failure at some $u$ characterizes the polynomials that are not encodings, since evaluation is injective on representatives of individual degree at most $q-1$ (Definition~\ref{def:polynomials-degree}); when $d \geq q$ it does not: for the admissible tuple $(q,m,d) = (8,1,8)$, the polynomial $g(x) = x^8$ is not an encoding, yet $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_1(u) = u = u^8 = g(u)$ for every $u \in \F_8$. Accordingly, the proofs below invoke the identity only for encodings; in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} the contribution of the remaining outcomes is controlled by the bound \eqref{eq:qld-nonencoding-mass} on the mass that the measurement of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7} places on polynomials that are not encodings, while in the conjugation identity \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6} the quantity $\mathrm{Dec}(g) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u)$ cancels exactly.

Its\n   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like\n   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example\n   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a\n   name ending in `_ofObligations`.\n6. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper\n   with `\\leanok`.\n\nWhen reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package\nhypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction\nand turn that content into a source-faithful lemma.  If the bridge does not\nactually follow from the paper hypotheses, do not preserve the paper theorem as\na strengthened statement.  Restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave\nthe missing proof obligation explicit, even if that means reintroducing a\ntracked `sorry` during a repair PR.\n\nSome side conditions are not deviations: positivity needed to define a\ndivision, nonemptiness of a finite type, decidability instances, field-model\ninstances, and similar boundary hypotheses may be faithful encodings of\nassumptions that the paper leaves implicit.  These should still be reviewed and\ndocumented if they are mathematically load-bearing.  The forbidden pattern is\ndifferent: moving an unproved step of the proof into the theorem statement, such\nas a `BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`,\n`Producer`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic `Assumptions` assumption that the\npaper theorem does not assume.  These assumptions\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\n\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\n`\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions.  A theorem\nwith an extra hypothesis such as\n`hbaseBridge : ... → MainFormalRepairedBridgeHypotheses ...` is temporary\nscaffolding at best; it must not be the declaration advertised as\n`thm:main-formal`.  The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\n\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\nintegrity audit:\n\n- paper assumptions;\n- Lean assumptions;\n- paper conclusion;\n- Lean conclusion;\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\n\n### Paper-realignment mode\n\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\n\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow.  It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\nnamed proof obligation.  Such a PR must:\n\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\n\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\n\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\n\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\nhypotheses.\n\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\nminimal form is:\n\n```text\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`.  Documented in\n`docs/paper-gaps/<note>.tex` or issue `#N`.  Elimination: prove\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\n```\n\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof.  Remove the marker only when the cited\ndeviation has been discharged.\n\nNot every discrepancy requires the full `**Unfaithful:**` marker.  If the paper\nhas a local typo, a documented numerical strengthening, or a genuine scope\nrestriction, use a lighter docstring marker such as `**Local fix:**` or\n`**Scope restriction:**`, citing the relevant paper-gap note.  These lighter\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\npaper hypotheses.\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Imports\n\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\n- One import per line\n- Follow existing local import style\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\n\n### File structure\n\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\n\n1. imports\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\n3. namespace / opens / variables\n4. declarations\n\n### Formatting\n\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\n  own line\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\n  theorem statement\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\n  tactic blocks.\n\n### Naming conventions\n\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\n\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\n\nProject-preferred variable names:\n\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\n- `σ` — strategies\n- `P` — projective measurements\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\n\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\n\n### Types and signatures\n\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\n  wrappers\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\n\n### Documentation\n\nRequired:\n\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\n- Cite blueprint nodes by their stable LaTeX label, for example blueprint\n  `lem:cl-concat`. Do not store blueprint line numbers in Lean docstrings. When\n  reviewing, derive the current span with\n  `python3 scripts/blueprint_citations.py resolve lem:cl-concat`.\n- Cite paper mirrors by a paper label when one exists, or by a repository path\n  plus a narrow anchored passage when the source has no suitable label. Paper\n  mirror line ranges are acceptable because those mirrors are immutable.\n\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\lean{...}`\nand `\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\n\n## Proof Engineering\n\n### Search before proving\n\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\n\n### Mathlib integration\n\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\n\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\n\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\n\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n### Validation ladder\n\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\n2. `lake build`\n\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\n\n### Lean-specific advice\n\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\n  already in the repo\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\n\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\n\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\nmathematical phrase is available.\n\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\npaper, and the local formalization. Do not invent slang or private shorthand for\nmathematical objects. The goal is prose that a third-party reader can understand\nwithout having read the agent conversation that produced the change.\n\n### Paper-gap notes\n\nFor the proof-gap terminology used to distinguish source theorems, internal\nproof obligations, and conditional helpers, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.  For documentation of discrepancies\nbetween the cited paper, the blueprint, and Lean, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. In particular, such notes should be\nmathematical prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists who have not\nread the issue discussion: introduce notation, state the cited assertion,\nisolate the calculation or logical obstruction, compare with the blueprint and\nLean statement, and give a clear verdict. If Lean uses a Mathlib result or\nconstruction not present in the cited argument, explain that replacement\npedagogically before naming the formal declaration. If the cited assertion is\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\n\n## Proof Integrity\n\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\n\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\n\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\n\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\n\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\n\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\n\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\n\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. Ask: *Can a real proof be built on top\nof this?*\n\n### Warnings\n\nPlaceholder tactics (`exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`) should be replaced\nwith concrete results. Debug artifacts (`dbg_trace`, `#check`, `#eval`,\n`#print`) should be removed from proof files. See the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference for\nthe full warning catalog.\n\n### Anti-patterns\n\nSubtler proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks yet still fail to\nprove the claimed mathematics are catalogued in `docs/anti_patterns.md`:\nconclusion-shaped hypotheses, definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback\nbranches, trivial default witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, and external\n`*Statement` smuggles. Reviewers should consult this file alongside\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md`.\n\n## PR and Commit Conventions\n\nPRs are GitHub pull requests (opened by `local/bin/pr_open.py`, merged by\n`local/bin/pr_merge.py`); `#N` in PR bodies and commit messages is the GitHub\nissue number. Titles, bodies, and commit rules below are unchanged from the\nparent project.\n\n### PR title format\n\n```\ntype(scope): short description\n```\n\n| Type       | When to use                                      |\n|------------|--------------------------------------------------|\n| `feat`     | New definition, lemma, theorem, or module         |\n| `fix`      | Bug fix (broken proof, wrong identifier, etc.)    |\n| `refactor` | Restructuring without changing API surface        |\n| `docs`     | Documentation or blueprint changes only           |\n| `style`    | Formatting, naming, or docstring cleanup only     |\n| `ci`       | CI/CD workflow changes                            |\n| `chore`    | Dependency bumps, linting, toolchain updates      |\n\n**Scope** is a shortened module path: `LDT/SelfImprovement`, `Quantum`,\n`blueprint`, etc. Omit the `MIPStarRE/` prefix.\n\n### PR body template\n\nEvery PR body must contain three sections:\n\n```markdown\n### Motivation\n- Why this change is needed. Cite the issue and paper/blueprint location.\n\n### Description\n- State precisely what changed.\n\n### Testing\n- What was verified and how (e.g., `lake build`, `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\"`).\n\n---\nAddresses #N\n```\n\nUse `Addresses #N` (keeps the issue open) or `Closes #N` (auto-closes on merge).\n\n### Commit messages\n\n- **Imperative mood** in the subject line (\"Add\", not \"Added\")\n- Subject under 72 characters\n- When squash-merging, the commit message should match the PR title format\n\n## Review Process\n\nEvery PR touching Lean code is reviewed by a dedicated local reviewer session\n(`local/bin/review.sh`, dispatched after green local CI; a session never\nreviews its own diff) against these criteria:\n\n1. **Proof correctness** — No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.\n2. **Mathlib style** — Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_doc` references.\n3. **Paper terminology** — Public Lean names and documentation should use\n   terminology from the paper and blueprint. See `docs/mathematical_language.md`.\n4. **Linter hygiene** — Fix warnings, don't mask them with broad\n   `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks.\n5. **Type safety** — No universe mismatches, coercion problems.\n6. **Performance** — Avoid expensive tactics on large types.\n7. **Modularity** — Are new lemmas general enough to be reused?\n8. **Documentation** — Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.\n9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** — Add `\\lean{}` and `\\leanok` tags for\n   formalized statements only when the Lean statement matches the source.\n   Record formalization-only auxiliary lemmas explicitly.\n10. **Scaffolding integrity** — Verify scaffolding aligns with Mathlib.\n11. **Statement drift** — Compare source-labelled theorem statements with the\n   paper and flag new hypotheses, weakened conclusions, changed quantifier\n   order, altered error parameters, or bridge/residual packages moving toward\n   a paper theorem.\n12. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** — Review against `docs/anti_patterns.md`.\n\nFor full details, see `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` and the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review` reference.\n\n## Blueprint and Documentation Work\n\nIf modifying blueprint material:\n\n- Keep chapter structure under `blueprint/src/chapter/`\n- Ensure `leanblueprint web` succeeds\n- Keep Lean declaration references valid\n- Sync theorem labels with Lean names\n- Add `\\lean{LeanDeclName}` and `\\leanok` tags for formalized statements\n\nFor blueprint style conventions, see `docs/blueprint_style_guide.md`.\n\nFor temporary conditional scaffolding and the `\\lean{}`/`\\leanok` tagging\nstrategy, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n## Agent Rule Sources\n\nChecked in this repository snapshot:\n\n- No `.cursorrules`\n- No Cloned files therefore do not\n   need their timestamps preserved.\n2. **A snapshot must never cross a keyhash boundary.** A `lean-toolchain` bump,\n   a Mathlib revision change, or a `lakefile.toml` edit is *total* invalidation.\n   `warm-worktree.sh` compares its own keyhash against the snapshot `STAMP`\n   before copying anything, and on mismatch refuses the clone, warns, and falls\n   back to the cold path. It never partially reuses.\n\n---\n\n## 4. On-disk layout\n\nShared packages and `hot-main` use `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT`; branch products may\nuse `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` as in §2. Neither runtime tree is committed.\n\n```\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/\n├── .full-build-lock/            # machine-wide: one full `lake build` at a time\n│   └── info                     # pid, host, started, started_epoch, purpose\n├── .telemetry-lock/             # short-lived; serializes JSONL appends\n├── logs/                        # captured build logs (warm-*.log, worktree-build-*.log)\n└── hot-main/\n    ├── .writer-lease/           # only the warmer holds this\n    │   └── info\n    ├── repo/                    # the always-warm detached checkout of main\n    ├── snapshots/\n    │   ├── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\n    │   │   ├── STAMP\n    │   │   └── build/           # a byte copy of repo/.lake/build\n    │   └── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\n    └── current -> snapshots/snap-<utc>-<sha12>   # absolute symlink\n```\n\nSnapshot names are `snap-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>-<sha12>` so that reverse\nlexicographic order *is* reverse chronological order — the GC needs no `stat`\ncalls and no name parsing.\n\n### `STAMP` schema\n\nA flat `key=value` file, one pair per line. It is **data, not code**: both scripts\nparse it with a whitelist and validate each value (`keyhash` must be 64 lowercase\nhex characters, `status ∈ {complete, partial}`, `sha` hex). Nothing in it is ever\n`eval`ed or `source`d.\n\n```\nsha=<full 40-char commit sha of the build>\nkeyhash=<64 hex chars, §3>\ntimestamp=<ISO 8601 with offset>\ntimestamp_epoch=<unix seconds>\nstatus=complete|partial\nbuild_seconds=<integer>\ntoolchain=<contents of lean-toolchain>\nsnapshot=<snapshot directory name>\nwarmer_version=1\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. The warmer — `cache-warmer.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh [--ref main | --sha <sha>] [--force] [--keep N]\n                          [--targets \"<lake targets>\"] [--lock-timeout S]\n                          [--lease-ttl S] [--gc-only] [--status]\n```\n\n### 5.1 Writer lease\n\nAcquired by `mkdir hot-main/.writer-lease` — `mkdir(2)` is the atomic\ntest-and-set. The lease directory holds an `info` file with `pid`, `host`,\n`started`, `started_epoch`, `purpose`.\n\nStaleness is decided in this order:\n\n* **Same host**: the holder's liveness is authoritative (`kill -0 pid`). A dead\n  pid means stale immediately; a live pid means *not* stale regardless of age.\n* **Different host, or no pid**: fall back to age > TTL (default 43200 s).\n\nThe TTL is deliberately much larger than the study map's suggested 3 h: this\nrepository's own cold full build took **25052 s** (`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`,\n2026-08-30). An age-only rule with a short TTL would break a live warmer's lease\nmid-build and produce exactly the concurrent-writer situation the lease exists to\nprevent.\n\n**Breaking a stale lock is done by renaming, not deleting.** Two processes that\nboth judge a lock stale will both attempt `mv lockdir lockdir.stale.<pid>.<epoch>`;\n`rename(2)` is atomic, so exactly one succeeds and proceeds to delete and\nre-acquire, while the loser loops and finds the lock freshly held. A\n`rm -rf && mkdir` sequence has no such guarantee.\n\n### 5.2 Build\n\n1. Clone or fetch `hot-main/repo` from the primary checkout; resolve `origin/<ref>`\n   first, then `<ref>` (`DESIGN.md` #8). Check out **detached** and forced.\n   `.lake/` is gitignored, so the checkout never touches the build tree, and\n   `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).\n2. Apply the fresh-state workaround (§8.2).\n3. Acquire the machine-wide full-build lock (§7) — **waiting, never aborting.**\n   This is the local reading of `pr-ci.yml:50`: a main build seeds the cache and\n   is never cancelled in favour of a newer commit. If main moves during a build,\n   finish, then warm again.\n4. `lake exe cache get` (failure is a warning, not fatal — the build simply\n   compiles more from source), then `lake build`, then any `--targets`.\n   **No `lake update`.**\n5. Everything is logged to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/logs/warm-<utc>-<sha12>.log`.\n   Telemetry records the log *path*, never log *content* — build output is\n   untrusted text (`DESIGN.md` #6) and does not belong in a data file that agent\n   prompts may later read.\n\n### 5.3 Atomic publish\n\nThe publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:\n\n1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with\n   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the\n   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).\n2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.\n3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.\n   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already\n   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**\n4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over\n   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).\n\n> Step 4 is done through `python3`, not `mv`. BSD `mv` `stat()`s its destination,\n> follows the existing `current` symlink to the directory it names, and would\n> move the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it. This is a real\n> trap, not a hypothetical one.\n\nConsumers exploit exactly this: they `readlink current` **once**, and hold the\nresolved concrete path for the rest of the run.\n\n### 5.4 Partial snapshots are intentional\n\nIf `lake build` fails, the warmer still publishes, with `status=partial`, and\nexits non-zero. This is `pr-ci.yml:161-162` ported directly: a broken `main`\ncommit must not stall every consumer at zero cache, and the modules that did\ncompile are still worth distributing. Consumers accept partial snapshots and say\nso loudly.\n\nA non-zero exit from the warmer therefore means *\"main did not build cleanly\"* —\nnot *\"nothing was published.\"* A cron wrapper should treat it as an alert, not a\nreason to retry.\n\n### 5.5 Retention\n\nKeep the newest `--keep` snapshots (default 2), the local analog of the parent's\n10 GB repository cache budget. **The snapshot `current` points to is never\ncollected**, even when it falls outside the keep window: a consumer that has\nresolved `current` must find a live directory. Abandoned `*.tmp` staging\ndirectories older than an hour are swept.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The consumer — `warm-worktree.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh [<worktree>] [--force] [--build] [--no-build]\n                           [--force-cold] [--skip-packages] [--status]\n```\n\nThe consumer is **read-only with respect to the cache**. It refuses outright to\noperate on any path inside `hot-main/repo` or `hot-main/snapshots`.\n\nDecision procedure:\n\n1. Compute the worktree's own keyhash (§3).\n2. Resolve `current` **once**; require `build/` and `STAMP` to exist.\n3. Read and validate the `STAMP`. A malformed stamp is treated as *no snapshot*.\n4. **Keyhash gate.** Mismatch → warn with both hashes, name the likely cause\n   (toolchain / manifest / lakefile change), point at the warmer, and take the\n   cold path. Never a partial reuse, never a silent skip.\n5. **Warm path**: `cp -c -R <snapshot>/build → <worktree>/.lake/build.incoming.$$`,\n   then `rename` into place. Write the idempotency marker\n   `<worktree>/.lake/.mipstarre-warm-stamp` recording the snapshot name, keyhash,\n   snapshot status and time. Then fetch tier 2 with `lake exe cache get`.\n   No full build unless `--build` is given — the point of the warm path is that\n   the agent's next incremental `lake build` compiles only its own delta.\n6. **Cold path**: `lake exe cache get`, then a full `lake build` under the\n   machine-wide lock (§7), unless `--no-build`.\n\n### 6.1 Idempotency and the do-not-clobber rule\n\nRe-running on an already-warmed worktree is a no-op for tier 1. Specifically:\n\n* marker snapshot **and** keyhash both match the resolved snapshot → skip the\n  clone;\n* `.lake/build` is populated but was **not** warmed from this snapshot → leave it\n  alone and warn. It may hold hours of an agent's incremental work; replacing it\n  with a main snapshot is destructive and is only done under `--force`.\n\n### 6.2 Why copy-on-write, and why not a symlink\n\nOn APFS, `cp -c -R` clones extents rather than bytes: the operation is near\ninstantaneous and initially consumes no additional space, with divergence paid\nfor only as the worktree's own build writes new blocks. This is what makes a\n*private writable copy per worktree* affordable — and a private writable copy is\nprecisely what preserves the single-writer invariant. A writable symlink or\nbind-style share of `.lake/build` across two concurrent `lake build` invocations\nis the local restatement of the parent's eviction bug and is never acceptable.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Concurrency: two locks, deliberately separate\n\n| lock | path | held by | protects |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| writer lease | `hot-main/.writer-lease` | the warmer only | the snapshot store and `hot-main/repo` |\n| full-build lock | `.full-build-lock` | warmer **and** consumers | RAM/CPU: one full `lake build` machine-wide |\n\nThey are separate so that a consumer's own full build can proceed while the\nwarmer sits idle between commits, and so that a warmer holding the writer lease\ndoes not block a consumer that only wants to *read* a published snapshot.\n\n`DESIGN.md` #7: **single-file `lake env lean <file>` checks take no lock.** They\nare read-only over existing oleans, which is exactly why the `.githooks/pre-push`\ngate uses them per changed file rather than a whole-library build. Do not add\nlocking there.\n\nThe parent's equivalent constraint was runner disk exhaustion, severe enough that\na CI job dropped Lean setup entirely and now only emits a notice\n(`pr-ci.yml:314`). Locally the binding resource is RAM during a Mathlib-scale\nbuild; the lock is the analog of a concurrency group.\n\nBoth locks use the same mkdir/rename-to-break protocol described in §5.1, with\nthe same liveness-first staleness rule, so a consumer and the warmer agree on\nwhat a stale lock is.\n\n### 7.1 Interoperating with `local/bin/ci.sh`\n\n`ci.sh` takes the same machine-wide full-build lock around its build step. Two\ncompatibility hazards follow, and both are handled here:\n\n* **Path.** All four takers — `cache-warmer.sh`, `warm-worktree.sh`, `ci.sh`,\n  and `housekeeping.sh`'s linter sweep — default the lock to\n  **`$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock`** and honour the override\n  **`MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK`**. One path, one mutex. (Historical note: the\n  first draft had `ci.sh` on `$CACHE_ROOT/hot-main/.full-build-lock` and the\n  sweep on a third flock — *two different paths are two independent mutexes,\n  and the invariant is silently void*; unified 2026-08-30, see\n  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.)\n* **Metadata layout.** `ci.sh` records its holder in `<lock>/owner` (pid, ISO\n  time, tag — one per line); these scripts record `<lock>/info` as `key=value`.\n  A script that cannot read the other's holder would conclude \"no pid, therefore\n  stale\" and break a *live* lock mid-build. Therefore: every acquisition here\n  writes **both** files, and staleness detection reads `info` first, then\n  `owner`, and falls back to the lock directory's mtime for age. An absent `host`\n  field is read as \"this host\", which keeps pid liveness authoritative.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Fresh-worktree bootstrap — `worktree-setup.sh`\n\nReplaces `.codex/setup.sh` (the Codex cloud environment hook) per `DESIGN.md`'s\nGitHub→local mapping. Order of operations:\n\n1. **Assert `elan`** — never install it by piping a URL into a shell. This is a\n   developer machine, not a disposable runner. Missing `elan` is a hard, actionable\n   error.\n2. **PATH**: `$HOME/.elan/bin` is exported for this process. The shell rc file is\n   modified **only** under `--persist-path`; otherwise the line to add is printed.\n3. **Toolchain guard**: `elan toolchain install $(cat lean-toolchain)`, once, only\n   if the pin is not already installed.\n4. **No `lake update`** — stated in the log, not silently omitted (§2).\n5. **`origin/main` check** (`DESIGN.md` #8): a warning, because the hooks and every\n   diff-based audit silently self-disable without it. Silent self-disabling is the\n   documented failure this check exists to surface.\n6. **Fresh-state workaround** (§8.2).\n7. **`warm-worktree.sh`** — invoked from the copy *next to this script*, not the\n   copy inside the worktree being bootstrapped. A worktree may hold an unreviewed\n   branch; the bootstrap must not execute code from the tree it is bootstrapping.\n   This is the local analog of `DESIGN.md` #5 (trusted prompts come from `main`).\n   If the consumer script is missing, this is a **hard error**: without it the\n   worktree would start cold, silently, which is the outcome the whole protocol\n   exists to prevent.\n8. **`scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`**, then `--check`. `docs/ci-automation.md`\n   calls out `--check` specifically for *\"each fresh worktree used for a PR.\"*\n\n`--check` is report-only and mutates nothing (`DESIGN.md` #10). It exits non-zero\nif anything is missing.\n\n### 8.1 Git environment hygiene\n\nEvery invocation of `lake` or of `git` inside a vendored package is wrapped in\n`run_outside_git_env`, ported from `.githooks/pre-push:19-25`: it unsets every\nvariable named by `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` in a subshell. Without it, a\nscript invoked from inside a git hook leaks `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` into\nLake's package checkouts, and nested git operations resolve the wrong repository.\n\n### 8.2 The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround\n\nKept verbatim in intent from `docgen.yml:56-69`, in all three scripts, because a\npristine agent worktree is exactly the fresh state that triggers it.\n\n*Upstream form.* `lake exe cache get` runs `lake update`, whose mathlib\npost-update hook prunes `.lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib` before\nfetching a cloud release. On a tree that has never built, the directory does not\nexist, and the uncaught exception aborts the **entire** cache fetch. Fix: create\nthe directory, but only if `proofwidgets` was actually checked out.\n\n*Local form.* The same fetch also aborts when a vendored package tree is\n**dirty**: build byproducts (`widget/js/lake.trace`) block the revision checkout.\nRecorded in `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, 2026-08-30 — a failed build followed\nby a successful retry after `git reset --hard` in the package. The scripts\ntherefore reset any vendored package tree with **tracked** modifications before\nfetching.\n\n`git clean` is deliberately **not** run inside a vendored package: it would delete\ndownloaded build output at a cost of hours. If an untracked byproduct still blocks\na checkout, the fetch fails loudly and the caller falls back to compiling from\nsource.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Telemetry\n\nEvery full build and every cache event appends one JSON line to\n`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, per `DESIGN.md`'s telemetry contract.\n\n```jsonc\n{\"ts\": \"<ISO 8601 with offset>\",\n \"kind\": \"warm\" | \"rebuild\" | \"cache-get\",\n \"trigger\": \"<who asked for this>\",\n \"outcome\": \"success\" | \"failed\",\n \"seconds\": <int>,\n \"sha\": \"<commit, when known>\",\n \"note\": \"<sanitized, ≤400 chars>\"}\n```\n\n* `warm` — a warmer build and publish.\n* `rebuild` — a consumer's full `lake build` (cold path, or `--build`).\n* `cache-get` — a per-worktree tier-2 fetch.\n\nThree properties are load-bearing:\n\n* **The primary checkout owns the file.** Even when invoked from a linked\n  worktree, the scripts resolve `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` back to the\n  primary repository, so an append-only JSONL does not fork per worktree and\n  produce merge conflicts. Override with `MIPSTARRE_TELEMETRY_DIR`.\n* **Appends are serialized** by a short-lived `mkdir` lock, and give up after 5 s\n  rather than delaying a build. Telemetry never blocks or fails a build; every\n  failure path degrades to a warning.\n* **`note` is sanitized** — non-printable characters stripped, truncated to 400\n  characters — because notes may quote build output, and compiler output is\n  untrusted text regardless of where it was produced (`DESIGN.md` #6).\n\n---\n\n## 10. Operating procedures\n\n```bash\n# Seed or refresh the hot main cache (do this after every merge to main).\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --ref main\n\n# What is published right now?\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --status\n\n# Bootstrap a brand-new agent worktree end to end.\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/.worktrees/issue-0042-qpbt-basis\n\n# Verify an existing worktree without touching it.\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/worktree --check\n\n# Re-warm a worktree after the warmer published a newer snapshot.\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --force\n\n# What would this worktree do, warm or cold?\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --status\n```\n\nAfter a toolchain or Mathlib bump lands on `main`, the ordering is fixed: **warm\nfirst, adopt second.** The bump changes the keyhash, so every existing snapshot\nis invalid and every worktree cold-paths until a fresh snapshot exists. Run\n`cache-warmer.sh --ref main` before dispatching agents, or pay for a full build in\neach worktree serialized behind one lock.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Failure modes and how each degrades\n\n| condition | behaviour |\n|---|---|\n| No snapshot published yet | Warn, name the warmer command, take the cold path. |\n| Keyhash mismatch | Warn with both hashes, take the cold path. Never a partial reuse. |\n| Malformed / unreadable `STAMP` | Treated as *no snapshot*; cold path. |\n| Snapshot is `partial` | Used, with a warning naming the SHA that failed. |\n| `cp -c` unsupported (non-APFS, cross-volume) | Warn, fall back to `cp -R`. Correct, just slower and larger. |\n| `lake exe cache get` fails | Warn; tier 2 gets compiled from source. Non-fatal. |\n| Full-build lock held | Wait; the warmer waits indefinitely by default, consumers time out per `--lock-timeout`. |\n| Stale lock (dead pid, or age > TTL) | Broken by atomic rename, with a warning naming the dead holder. |\n| Primary repo has no commits on `main` | Hard error naming the cause. Never a silent no-op. |\n| `warm-worktree.sh` missing during bootstrap | Hard error. `--skip-warm` is the explicit opt-out. |\n| `origin/main` does not resolve | Warning, non-zero exit from `--check`, because hooks self-disable silently. |\n| `python3` absent | Warmer: hard error (needed for the atomic publish). Consumer: warning, telemetry skipped. |\n\n---\n\n## 12. Invariant checklist\n\nA change to any of these scripts must preserve all of the following:\n\n1. Only `cache-warmer.sh` writes into `hot-main/`. Never a silent no-op.\n# Protocol — local PR CI\n\nNormative protocol for `local/bin/ci.sh`, the local replacement for\n`.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml` (frozen under `.github/`, never executed here).\nRead `meta.md` first; `build-cache.md` owns the hot-main cache this protocol\nconsumes but never writes.\n\n`ci.sh <pr-number>` is the **only** thing allowed to publish the `local-ci/*`\ncommit statuses. Everything downstream — `review.sh` (invariant 2: review only\nafter green CI on the same head SHA), `autofix.sh` (invariant 3: sync/audit\nfailures are never auto-fixed), and the merge gate in `pr_merge.py` — reads\nthose exact-head statuses and the manifest comment this script publishes\n(`local/protocols/issues-prs.md` §2), and nothing else.\n\n## 1. What it is\n\nThe parent repository consolidated seven workflows into one so that a pull\nrequest produces exactly **one** CI completion event, which the auto-fix\ndispatcher keys off (`pr-ci.yml:3-8`). The local port keeps that property: one\ninvocation, one manifest, one exit code.\n\n```\nlocal/bin/ci.sh <pr-id> [--worktree PATH] [--base REF] [--only STEP]\n                        [--force-all] [--skip-build] [--dry-run]\n```\n\n`<pr-id>` is the GitHub PR number; the script reads `branch`, `base` and the\nhead SHA from GitHub (`gh_common.py pr-view`), finds the branch's worktree (via\n`git worktree list`, falling back to `.worktrees/<branch with / → ->`), and\nruns everything **inside that worktree**. Nothing is run in the primary\ncheckout, and the worktree's branch tip must equal the remote head before the\nrun starts.\n\nExit status: `0` all gating steps passed or were legitimately skipped; `1` at\nleast one gating step failed or could not run; `2` the run could not start\n(unknown PR number, missing worktree, unresolvable base, GitHub unreachable —\na GitHub error never degrades to a local record).\n\n### Preconditions that are hard errors, never silent skips\n\n| Precondition | Why it is fatal |\n|---|---|\n| GitHub returns an open PR with a head branch | there is no branch to test |\n| a worktree for that branch exists | CI must not test the primary checkout |\n| `origin/<base>` or `<base>` resolves | invariant 8 — the diff-based audits and the change gating self-disable without a base, which is exactly the \"checks silently stopped running\" failure the parent repo patched twice |\n| a merge base exists | the change set is undefined without one |\n| `python3` on `PATH` | every audit job and the manifest writer need it |\n\nThere is deliberately **no `LOCAL_CI_ENABLED` kill switch**. `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED`\nand `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` exist because a disabled reviewer or fixer merely\nstops work from happening; a disabled CI would hand the merge gate a green\nlight it never earned. If CI must not run, do not run it — the head SHA simply\nkeeps whatever statuses it already carries.\n\n## 2. If `.lake/build` is absent, run `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh <worktree>`,\n   which resolves the hot-main snapshot and clones it copy-on-write. Trust boundary\n\nTwo things about `ci.sh` are worth stating plainly.\n\n**It executes branch-authored code.** The audit scripts, the test suite, and\n`lakefile.toml` all come from the worktree under test, because that is what CI\nmeans and what the parent workflow did. a **missing** context blocks, because GitHub's combined state\n   reads `success` for a commit carrying no statuses at all;\n4. that SHA's marker-bound `COMMENT` review (or one carried forward per\n   review.md §13) carries `VERDICT: APPROVED`, or\n   `COMMENTED` with zero unchecked findings, **and** `local-review/summary` is\n   `success` there;\n5. no `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review stands on that head, from anyone;\n6. no live fix lock for the branch (`locks/fix-<branch>.lock`, running holder);\n   the count of `merge-base..head` commits whose subject starts with a §1 fix\n   prefix is printed for the record and is not a gate;\n7. every issue the PR body closes — all nine of GitHub's closing keywords, not\n   just `Closes` — has no open sub-issue left.\n\n`--adjudicated` waives gate 4's adverse verdict and nothing else, and only when\nan exact-head `ADJUDICATION` comment backs it; gate 5 is never adjudicable.\n\nAfterwards a best-effort, non-fatal tail fast-forwards local `main` to the\nremote merge commit; branch and worktree cleanup keeps its safeguards (local\ndirt defers it with a warning).\n\n### Main-cycle integration checkpoint\n\nThe active owner service records, at each bounded tick, the local `main` SHA,\nthe readable remote `refs/heads/main` SHA, primary cleanliness, transport\nresult, and the age and exact head of the oldest CI-and-review-eligible open\nPR. A dirty primary, remote mismatch, unavailable transport, active fix or\ntransaction lock, missing configured Space allocation or external-zero gate, or a stale\ncandidate is\na HOLD reason; it is never silently converted into a merge attempt. After a\nsuccessful daemon-owned merge, the service re-reads remote `main` and records\nthe new SHA before the next tick. The service may invoke `pr_merge.py` only as\nits daemon-owned final action after these checks; workers never merge directly.\nEach tick has bounded Git/GitHub reads and records failures as HOLD rather than\nexiting the loop. The cadence is monotonic: work time is subtracted from the\nconfigured interval (default 300 seconds). Candidate records distinguish stale\nexact-head PRs from fresh actionable PRs; `pr_age_s` is PR creation age, while\neligibility onset remains unknown unless separately observed.\n\n## 4. Read `local/protocols/meta.md` first: it\ngoverns how this document changes and what must be recorded when it does.\n\nReplaces `.github/workflows/pr-review.yml` — the `gate`, `code-review` and\n`prose-review` jobs — together with the review half of the `@claude` /\n`@codex` mention system documented in `docs/pr_review_management.md`.
